newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: No early redemption Hoogovens 2001 bond.
newsitem.headline: No early redemption Hoogovens 2001 bond.

text.p: Steel and aluminium group Koninklijke Hoogovens NV said on Tuesday it did not plan an early redemption of its 4.5 percent 1994-2001 subordinated convertible bond issue.

The company earlier announced it would issue a 300 million guilders 10 year subordinated convertible bond. The coupon will be announced after closing of the subscriptions on April 18 and is expected to be between 4.5 and 4.875 percent.
"The net proceeds from the bond issue will strengthen Hoogovens' capital structure and therefore its competitive position," the company said in a statement.

The new bonds can be converted into Hoogovens shares from April 24, 2000, at a price which will be announced after closing of subscriptions and will be 15 to 20 percent higher than Hoogovens' current share price on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
Hoogovens said the issue could be increased through a "greenshoe option" by a maximum of 15 percent, which would raise the proceeds to 345 million guilders.

The banking syndicate is led by ABN AMRO Rothschild and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell as joint global coordinators. SBC Warburg is senior co-lead manager and ING Barings and Rabo Securities are co-lead managers.
